::: {.why}
Monitoring everything produces alerts you ignore, and the list you wrote last night is short enough that each item can have a real check behind it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement a monitor for each of the four failure modes, with a threshold you can defend.
- Say what each monitor's false positive rate is and why you chose that threshold.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement the four: data freshness against the exchange calendar, position drift between intended and actual, fill price against the expected price, and signal values against their historical distribution. Each returns a status and a number rather than a boolean, so a near-miss is visible.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Set the thresholds from history rather than by feel: run each monitor over your backtest period and choose a threshold with a false positive rate you would tolerate, stated as alerts per month. A monitor that would have fired forty times last year is one you will disable in February.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Four monitors with thresholds calibrated against historical data run alongside the daily pipeline, each reporting a number rather than a boolean so that near-misses are visible before they become failures.
:::

:::
